description.purpose: The intake that turns a structural wish into a MANIFEST -- an ordered list of mutation declarations, ready to be submitted by whoever asked for it. Two classes on one lane: a FAST LANE of predefined parameterised recipes that runs without calling a model at all, and a DESIGN LANE that consults the builder's own corpus and asks one. Since 1.2.0 the fast lane also renders a LEVEL -- the transit edge set a new organisation, member, assistant, channel, screen or app gets from its parent is the same set every time, so it is a table rather than a paragraph a model rewrites per build. Since 1.3.0 a level can also be grown ASLEEP (`birth`, and a channel is asleep by default), and an assistant can be grown with the identity door beside it (`subscribe`) -- the push edge that lets the member's own record reach the new agent's prompt. Since 1.4.1 a container level ADDRESSES its children: the six doors an organisation or a member gets carry `context.org` / `context.member` beside the lane, permissively -- so a second child of one container is a second address rather than a second delivery. Since 1.4.0 the design lane's briefing publishes the form of `add_templates` and its own round budget: a wish whose class the catalogue does not carry is answered by WRITING that class into the same manifest rather than by searching for one that does not exist, and whether an authored cell is accepted stays the submitter's `code.author` question. It never applies anything: no cell in this template has an edge onto the control plane, which is a property of the files rather than a promise in this text. Since 1.4.1 the design lane's loop is one the model can see the end of: every re-briefing carries the round it is in and what is left of it, the LAST round is a writing round asked with no tool menu at all, and a build that still ends at the cap says `design_budget_exhausted` instead of naming whatever the last turn happened to be. The corpus behind it carries what the briefing demands exactness about -- the six rendered level edge sets and every shipped store's tables and columns -- so a lookup can end. Since 1.4.2 the TEMPLATES block names the root `config.json` as an obligation rather than leaving it to "one config.json per cell": that root file is what an instance of a registered class IS, and a class whose cells live only in subdirectories is refused at the entry (#509). Since 1.4.3 a grown LEVEL declares itself AT the container it grows into -- scope `/os/orgs` for an organisation, `<member>/assistants` for an assistant -- and names its child bare: the same tree and the same absolute edges, but a scope root the shipped broker rule already permits, so the FIRST organisation of a colony is buildable through the front door instead of only by an operator (#503). The one exception is the identity door, which reaches a SIBLING of the container and keeps the wider declaration, because neither `..` in an edge endpoint nor a second declaration that creates nothing is accepted anywhere on that road. Since 1.5.0 the hive path takes a fourth lane, and it is pure TRANSIT: `in_ingest` goes straight to the librarian this template refs and the reconciliation report comes back out on `catalogue`, paired in `required_drains`. The corpus is a SEED, so a class registered after this colony was born is resolvable at the mutation door and invisible to the composer; the one caller that knows both that a manifest committed and that its diff registered a class is the submitter, which stands outside this hive -- and an edge from there to a cell inside it crosses two seals, so the lane exists at the hive path or not at all (#504). A grown CHANNEL is also TOLD the round its turns are spoken in rather than inventing it: `ctx.member_person` is required for that level, the round literal is built from it and from the `assistant` the wish named, and a wish that does not say who the person is comes back as `wish_incomplete` with the question. The identity used to be read off the member's DIRECTORY name, and a directory that is not spelled like the person made the audience gate refuse every row of that person's memory, in every leg, behind a bundle that reads exactly like an empty store (#517). Since 1.5.2 two of this hive's occupants are named after the templates they reference rather than after the roles they play: `dispatcher` and `builder-librarian`, where the tree said `dispatch` and `librarian` (#545). A ref onto template X is a directory called X, so an edge and the library spell the same word; a mutation that named `<builder>/dispatch` or `<builder>/librarian` stops resolving, and that is the whole of the migration.
description.use_when: Once per colony, at the OS level, beside the capability broker and the control loop -- a level owns what its siblings must share (ADR-0013), and one baumeister, one corpus and one audit trail is exactly what every organisation under it shares. Reached on `in_build` at the hive path; the draft comes back on `manifest`, a refusal on `error`.
description.not_in_scope: No application, no mutation, no rescan, no write to disk of any kind -- the requester submits, under its own identity, through the submitter that stands beside this hive. No approval decision either: whether a draft may be applied is decided where it is submitted, not where it is drawn. And no second corpus: retrieval is `builder-librarian`, referenced, not copied.
examples: hop.build_op == 'draft' with a known `recipe` -> the fast lane renders the manifest deterministically, no model, no network
"grow an assistant named scribe from <a template> under <a member path>" -> recognised as the grow_level recipe, one declaration, fourteen edges, still no model
a plain-language request with no recipe -> librarian brief -> one model call -> a normalised manifest plus its sha256 digest
a request the composer answers with prose and no JSON -> `error`, error_code `no_manifest_in_answer`, and the build stops rather than shipping an empty one
a request that names no model where the template demands one -> the composer ASKS instead of inventing a literal, and the question comes back on `error` as `wish_incomplete`
"grow a channel named telegram from <a connector> under <a member path>" -> the node is rendered `birth: inactive`: registered, addressable, and not polling anything until a second act arms it

the same channel wish with no person named -> nothing is rendered: `error`, error_code `wish_incomplete`, and the question comes back in the words whoever made the wish has to answer. A round is provenance, and a guessed one blanks the whole memory behind a gate that is working exactly as specified
"grow a member named alex from <a template> under <an org path>" -> eighteen edges, and the six doors among them name alex: a container with two members is two addresses, not one broadcast

a wish for a unit no template carries -> the composer registers the class with `add_templates` and instantiates it in the SAME manifest, because that operation runs first in its diff; the submitter then asks `code.author` and a colony that says no answers `code_author_denied`

a wish the composer keeps looking for -- the last round is offered no tools at all, so the answer is the manifest; if a round cap still fires it comes back as `design_budget_exhausted` naming the rounds spent, never as "your answer was not a list"

a committed manifest that registered a class -> the shell re-stamps the submitter's receipt onto `in_ingest` here, the librarian reconciles its corpus against `/colony/templates`, and the report leaves on `catalogue`: measured, `catalogue_known 43`, `catalogue_ingested 4`, and a `catalogue_lookup` for the new name answers "the request names templates that exist" where it said "no template by that name" one message earlier
